subproblem.title: Good slicing radii in the dyadic intervals ((1/2)^{j+3}, (1/2)^{j+2})
subproblem.statement: Assume, as a hypothesis of the statement, (GR), the frozen type of Submission.cmcsd_good_radius: for P ∈ ℕ, finite measures μ, μ′ on ℝ^P (IsFiniteMeasure), f : ℝ^P → ℝ measurable, a real ρ > 0 and B ∈ [0, ∞] with μ({f < ρ}) ≤ B, there is r with ρ/2 < r < ρ, liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ({r − h < f < r}) ≤ ofReal(4/ρ)·B and liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ′({r − h < f < r}) < ∞ (liminf along the filter 𝓝[>] 0, values in [0, ∞]). Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let μ, μ′ be finite measures on ℝ^P, d : ℝ^P → ℝ measurable, C ∈ ℝ≥0 and M, M′ ∈ [0, ∞] with M ≠ ∞ and M′ ≠ ∞, and assume that for every real r with 0 < r ≤ 1/4, μ({d < r}) ≤ C·ofReal(r^{m+2})·M and μ′({d < r}) ≤ C·ofReal(r^{m+2})·M′ (in [0, ∞], ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal). Then there is r : ℕ → ℝ such that: (i) (1/2)^{j+3} < r_j < (1/2)^{j+2} for every j ∈ ℕ; (ii) r is strictly decreasing; (iii) for every j, μ({d < r_j}) ≤ C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)})·M and μ′({d < r_j}) ≤ C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)})·M′; (iv) μ({d < r_j}) → 0 and μ′({d < r_j}) → 0 as j → ∞; (v) for every j, liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ({r_j − h < d < r_j}) ≤ 4·C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+1)})·M; (vi) for every j, liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ′({r_j − h < d < r_j}) < ∞. Here liminf is taken along the filter 𝓝[>] 0 of right neighbourhoods of 0, and {r_j − h < d < r_j} = {x : r_j − h < d(x) ∧ d(x) < r_j}.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent-supplied proof of cmcsd_shell_decomposition, with the density estimates of its steps 11(b) and 13(iii); Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, proof of the deformation theorem 5.1, displays (8)–(10) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1405–1928) (display (10): ρ ∈ (σ/2, σ) with M⟨T, d, ρ⟩ ≤ (c/σ)·M(T_σ − T_{σ/2})).
1. Put ρ_j := (1/2)^{j+2}. Then ρ_j > 0, ρ_j ≤ (1/2)^2 = 1/4 (pow_le_pow_of_le_one, since j + 2 ≥ 2) and ρ_j/2 = (1/2)^{j+3} (pow_succ).
2. (Choice of r_j; (i) and (vi).) Fix j and put B_j := C·ofReal(ρ_j^{m+2})·M. By the hypothesis with r := ρ_j, μ({d < ρ_j}) ≤ B_j. GR, applied with μ, μ′ (finite), f := d (measurable), ρ := ρ_j > 0 and B := B_j, gives r_j with ρ_j/2 < r_j < ρ_j, liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ({r_j − h < d < r_j}) ≤ ofReal(4/ρ_j)·B_j and liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ′({r_j − h < d < r_j}) < ∞. Choose such an r_j for every j (axiom of choice). By step 1 this gives (i), and (vi) holds.
3. ((ii).) For every j, r_{j+1} < (1/2)^{j+3} < r_j by (i) (applied to j + 1 and to j). Hence r is strictly decreasing (strictAnti_nat_of_succ_lt).
4. ((iii).) Since r_j < ρ_j, {d < r_j} ⊆ {d < ρ_j}, so μ({d < r_j}) ≤ μ({d < ρ_j}) ≤ C·ofReal(ρ_j^{m+2})·M by the hypothesis with r := ρ_j, and ρ_j^{m+2} = ((1/2)^{j+2})^{m+2} = (1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)} (pow_mul). The same argument with μ′ and M′ gives the second inequality.
5. ((iv).) Since (j + 2)(m + 2) ≥ j → ∞ and (1/2)^n → 0 (tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one), (1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)} → 0, hence ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)}) → ofReal 0 = 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal). As C ≠ ∞ and M ≠ ∞, C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)})·M → C·0·M = 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul, ENNReal.Tendsto.mul_const). By (iii), 0 ≤ μ({d < r_j}) ≤ C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)})·M, so μ({d < r_j}) → 0 (tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le). The same argument with μ′ and M′ ≠ ∞ gives μ′({d < r_j}) → 0.
6. ((v).) For ρ > 0 we have (4/ρ)·ρ^{m+2} = 4ρ^{m+1}, hence ofReal(4/ρ)·ofReal(ρ^{m+2}) = ofReal(4ρ^{m+1}) = 4·ofReal(ρ^{m+1}) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul with 4/ρ ≥ 0 and with 4 ≥ 0; ENNReal.ofReal_ofNat). Using commutativity and associativity of multiplication in [0, ∞], ofReal(4/ρ_j)·B_j = C·(ofReal(4/ρ_j)·ofReal(ρ_j^{m+2}))·M = 4·C·ofReal(ρ_j^{m+1})·M, and ρ_j^{m+1} = (1/2)^{(j+2)(m+1)} (pow_mul). With the liminf bound of step 2 this gives (v). ∎
proof_key_steps: GR with B_j = C·ofReal(ρ_j^{m+2})·M (density hypothesis at ρ_j) gives r_j ∈ (ρ_j/2, ρ_j) with both liminf bounds; choose for all j.
r_{j+1} < (1/2)^{j+3} < r_j, so r is strictly decreasing.
μ({d < r_j}) ≤ μ({d < ρ_j}) ≤ C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)})·M (pow_mul), and the same for μ′; this bound tends to 0.
ofReal(4/ρ)·ofReal(ρ^{m+2}) = 4·ofReal(ρ^{m+1}) turns the GR bound into 4·C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+1)})·M.

audit.reason: GR is applied with exactly its stated hypotheses at positive radii at most 1/4. The chosen intervals imply strict decrease, measure monotonicity gives both density bounds, finite M and M′ justify convergence to zero, and the positive-radius algebra gives the exact factor 4 and exponent m+1.

subproblem.title: The mass measure of a current on ℝ^P vanishes off the support of the current
subproblem.statement: Assume, as a hypothesis of the statement, (VO), the frozen type of Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) whose tsupport is disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0. Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) (a current on U = univ) and let μ be a measure on ℝ^P such that M_W(X) = μ(W) for every open set W ⊆ ℝ^P. Then μ(ℝ^P \ spt X) = 0, i.e. μ((spt X)ᶜ) = 0. Conventions (as in the frozen contract and SimonGMT Chapter06): ℝ^P = Euclid P (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)). For U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^k(U) = TestFormOn U k (smooth k-forms on ℝ^P whose compact tsupport lies in U) and 𝒟_k(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U k; X(ω) is the value of X on ω; X − Y is the contract subtraction, (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) − Y(ω) (definitional); 0 is the zero current; ∂X = X.boundary with ∂X(η) = X(dη) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply); currents with equal values are equal (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). Λ_k = MultiVector P k (continuous linear functionals on k-covectors) and |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α (Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector). M_G(X) = X.massOn G ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over the ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (massAdmissibleOn U k G); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X); boundaryMassOn X G = M_G(∂X) if k ≥ 1 and 0 if k = 0. spt X = X.support = U \ X.zeroRegion, where X.zeroRegion is the union of the open W with compact closure contained in U on which X vanishes (X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W). Integrals ∫_E g dμ are Bochner integrals over μ⌞E; {d < t} abbreviates {x : d(x) < t}.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → ∀ (P k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → X.massOn W = μ W) → μ X.supportᶜ = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step (1d) of the parent-supplied proof of cmcsd_shell_decomposition (used there for T and, in step 2, for ∂T); Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, proof of the deformation theorem 5.1, displays (8)–(10) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1405–1928).
1. (The complement of the support is the open zero region.) By definition, spt X = ℝ^P \ Z with Z := X.zeroRegion, the union of all open W with compact closure (contained in ℝ^P) on which X vanishes. Hence (spt X)ᶜ = Z (the complement of univ \ Z is Z), and Z is open, being a union of open sets (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion).
2. By the hypothesis applied to the open set W := Z, μ((spt X)ᶜ) = μ(Z) = M_Z(X), and by definition M_Z(X) is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over the ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) admissible for M_Z (tsupport ω ⊆ Z and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x).
3. Let ω be admissible for M_Z. Then tsupport ω ⊆ Z = (spt X)ᶜ, so tsupport ω is disjoint from spt X (Set.disjoint_of_subset_left with disjoint_compl_left). By (VO), applied with U := ℝ^P and S := X, X(ω) = 0, hence ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) = ENNReal.ofReal 0 = 0.
4. Every element of the set whose supremum is M_Z(X) is therefore 0, so M_Z(X) ≤ 0 (sSup_le), i.e. M_Z(X) = 0. By step 2, μ((spt X)ᶜ) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: (spt X)ᶜ = X.zeroRegion, which is open (isOpen_zeroRegion).
μ((spt X)ᶜ) = M_Z(X), the supremum of ofReal X(ω) over ω admissible for Z = X.zeroRegion.
Every such ω has tsupport disjoint from spt X, so X(ω) = 0 by (VO).
The supremum is ≤ 0 (sSup_le), so μ((spt X)ᶜ) = 0.

audit.reason: The prose and type agree. On univ, the support complement is the open zero region. VO annihilates every admissible evaluation there, so its mass and hence its measure vanish. No finiteness or additional support lemma is silently assumed.

Source: the boundary-mass bookkeeping of step 12 of the parent-supplied proof of cmcsd_shell_decomposition ((X − Y).boundary = ∂X − ∂Y, ∂∂ = 0, M(0) = 0 and MS). Sibling used: MS = mass_sub (cmc_fc_cs_massOn_sub_le: M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B) for all U, G and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U)).
1. (M_G(0) = 0 in every degree.) M_G(0) is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal 0(ω) = ENNReal.ofReal 0 = 0 over the admissible ω (GeometricCurrentOn.zero_apply), so M_G(0) ≤ 0 (sSup_le), i.e. M_G(0) = 0.
2. (m = 0.) boundaryMassOn of any current of degree 0 is 0 by definition. So (a) reads 0 ≤ 0 + 0, and (b), for the 0-current ∂X, reads 0 = 0.
3. (m = k + 1, part (a).) For Z ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), boundaryMassOn Z G = M_G(∂Z) by definition. For η ∈ 𝒟^k(U), ∂(X − Y)(η) = (X − Y)(dη) = X(dη) − Y(dη) = ∂X(η) − ∂Y(η) = (∂X − ∂Y)(η) (all definitional), so ∂(X − Y) = ∂X − ∂Y (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). By MS (with k, U, G, ∂X, ∂Y), M_G(∂(X − Y)) = M_G(∂X − ∂Y) ≤ M_G(∂X) + M_G(∂Y), which is (a).
4. (m = k + 1, part (b).) For X ∈ 𝒟_{k+2}(U), ∂X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) and boundaryMassOn (∂X) G = M_G(∂∂X) = M_G(0) = 0 by GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary and step 1. ∎

Degree 0: boundaryMassOn is identically 0.
Degree k + 1: ∂(X − Y) = ∂X − ∂Y (ext), then MS.

subproblem.title: Dyadic shells of a current represented by a finite measure: shell integrals, convergence of the shell series, supports and masses
subproblem.statement: Assume, as hypotheses of the statement, (S), the frozen type of Submission.cmcsd_support_calculus: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, (i) if E ⊆ ℝ^P is closed and X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) satisfies X(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) whose tsupport is disjoint from E, then spt X ⊆ E; (ii) spt X is closed for every X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P); (iii) spt(A − B) ⊆ spt A ∪ spt B for A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P); (iv) spt 0 = ∅; (v) spt ∂A ⊆ spt A for A ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P); and (ML), the frozen type of Submission.cmcsd_massOn_le_measure_inter: for P, d ∈ ℕ, any U ⊆ ℝ^P, X ∈ 𝒟_d(U), a measure μ, ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_d and sets E, V ⊆ ℝ^P, if |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every d-covector α for μ-a.e. x and X(ω) = ∫_E ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U), then M_V(X) ≤ μ(E ∩ V). Let P, k ∈ ℕ, X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P), A, Y : ℕ → 𝒟_k(ℝ^P), μ a measure on ℝ^P, ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_k, d : ℝ^P → ℝ and r : ℕ → ℝ. Assume: μ is a finite measure; ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable; for μ-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every k-covector α; μ(ℝ^P \ spt X) = 0; d is continuous; r is strictly decreasing (StrictAnti); μ({d < r_j}) → 0 as j → ∞; X(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x), A_j(ω) = ∫_{d<r_j} ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) (for every j), Y_0(ω) = X(ω) − A_0(ω) and Y_{j+1}(ω) = A_j(ω) − A_{j+1}(ω) (for every j), for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P). Then, for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) and j ∈ ℕ: (a) Y_0(ω) = ∫_{r_0≤d} ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) and Y_{j+1}(ω) = ∫_{r_{j+1}≤d<r_j} ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x), the domains being {x : r_0 ≤ d(x)} and {x : r_{j+1} ≤ d(x) ∧ d(x) < r_j}; (b) Σ_j Y_j(ω) = X(ω) (HasSum (j ↦ Y_j(ω)) (X(ω))); (c) spt Y_j ⊆ spt X ∩ {x : r_j ≤ d(x)} and spt A_j ⊆ spt X; (d) M(Y_0) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) and M(Y_{j+1}) ≤ μ({d < r_j}). Conventions (as in the frozen contract and SimonGMT Chapter06): ℝ^P = Euclid P (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)). For U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^k(U) = TestFormOn U k (smooth k-forms on ℝ^P whose compact tsupport lies in U) and 𝒟_k(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U k; X(ω) is the value of X on ω; X − Y is the contract subtraction, (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) − Y(ω) (definitional); 0 is the zero current; ∂X = X.boundary with ∂X(η) = X(dη) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply); currents with equal values are equal (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). Λ_k = MultiVector P k (continuous linear functionals on k-covectors) and |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α (Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector). M_G(X) = X.massOn G ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over the ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (massAdmissibleOn U k G); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X); boundaryMassOn X G = M_G(∂X) if k ≥ 1 and 0 if k = 0. spt X = X.support = U \ X.zeroRegion, where X.zeroRegion is the union of the open W with compact closure contained in U on which X vanishes (X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W). Integrals ∫_E g dμ are Bochner integrals over μ⌞E; {d < t} abbreviates {x : d(x) < t}.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3, 6, 7, 10(a)–(b), 11 and 13 of the parent-supplied proof of cmcsd_shell_decomposition, stated for a general current represented by a finite measure (the parent applies it to (T, μ_T, ξ, A_{r_j}, W_j) and to (∂T, μ_∂, ξ_∂, B_{r_j}, D_j)); Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, proof of the deformation theorem 5.1, displays (8)–(10) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1405–1928). Sibling used: EB = eval_mass_bound (cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn: if M_W(Z) ≠ ∞, tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ c for all x, then |Z(ω)| ≤ c·M_W(Z).toReal).
Notation. For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) put f_ω(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)). Put E_0 := {x : r_0 ≤ d(x)} and E_{j+1} := {x : r_{j+1} ≤ d(x) ∧ d(x) < r_j}. As d is continuous, {d < t} is open, {t ≤ d} is closed, and all these sets are Borel (measurableSet_lt, measurableSet_le).
1. (Bound for a test form.) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P). The map x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous: ω is smooth, hence continuous, and α ↦ |α| = √(Σ_I [I strictly increasing] α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(k)})²) is continuous because each evaluation α ↦ α(v) is continuous (continuous_eval_const) and finite sums, squares and Real.sqrt are continuous. It vanishes outside the compact set tsupport ω (|0| = 0, covectorEuclideanNorm_zero; HasCompactSupport.comp_left). Hence it is bounded (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support): there is c_ω with |ω(x)| ≤ c_ω for every x, and c_ω ≥ |ω(0)| ≥ 0.
2. (Integrability.) f_ω is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, as the image of the pair (ξ, ω), with ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable and ω continuous, under the continuous evaluation map (L, α) ↦ L(α) (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂ with isBoundedBilinearMap_apply.continuous). For μ-a.e. x, |f_ω(x)| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ c_ω by the a.e. bound on ξ and step 1. As μ is finite, f_ω is μ-integrable (Integrable.of_bound), hence integrable on every set.
3. ((a) Shell integrals.) j = 0: {d < r_0}ᶜ = {r_0 ≤ d} = E_0, so by integral_add_compl (step 2) Y_0(ω) = X(ω) − A_0(ω) = ∫ f_ω dμ − ∫_{d<r_0} f_ω dμ = ∫_{E_0} f_ω dμ. j + 1: as r_{j+1} < r_j, {d < r_{j+1}} ⊆ {d < r_j}, and {d < r_j} \ {d < r_{j+1}} = {r_{j+1} ≤ d ∧ d < r_j} = E_{j+1}; so by setIntegral_sdiff (step 2) Y_{j+1}(ω) = ∫_{d<r_j} f_ω dμ − ∫_{d<r_{j+1}} f_ω dμ = ∫_{E_{j+1}} f_ω dμ. This is (a); thus Y_j(ω) = ∫_{E_j} f_ω dμ for every j.
4. (Shell geometry.) E_j ⊆ {r_j ≤ d} for every j. If i < j then j = j′ + 1 with j′ ≥ i, and E_j ⊆ {d < r_{j′}} ⊆ {d < r_i} since r is decreasing. Hence for i < j no x lies in E_i ∩ E_j (it would satisfy r_i ≤ d(x) < r_i): the E_j are pairwise disjoint Borel sets.
5. ((d) Masses.) By ML with U := ℝ^P, E := E_j and V := ℝ^P (the a.e. bound on ξ and the formula of step 3), M(Y_j) = M_{ℝ^P}(Y_j) ≤ μ(E_j ∩ ℝ^P) = μ(E_j); likewise, by ML with E := {d < r_j} and the hypothesis on A_j, M(A_j) ≤ μ({d < r_j}). In particular M(Y_0) ≤ μ(E_0) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) and M(Y_{j+1}) ≤ μ(E_{j+1}) ≤ μ({d < r_j}) because E_{j+1} ⊆ {d < r_j}. This is (d).
6. (Evaluation bound.) Let Z ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) and G ⊆ ℝ^P with M(Z) ≤ μ(G). Then M(Z) ≤ μ(G) < ∞ (μ finite), so EB with U = W := ℝ^P, r := c_ω (tsupport ω ⊆ ℝ^P, step 1) gives |Z(ω)| ≤ c_ω·M(Z).toReal ≤ c_ω·μ(G).toReal (ENNReal.toReal_mono, c_ω ≥ 0).
7. (Summability.) By step 4 and countable additivity (measure_iUnion), Σ_j μ(E_j) = μ(⋃_j E_j) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) < ∞, so (μ(E_j).toReal)_j is summable (ENNReal.summable_toReal). By steps 5 and 6, |Y_j(ω)| ≤ c_ω·μ(E_j).toReal, so (Y_j(ω))_j is summable (Summable.of_norm_bounded).
8. (Partial sums.) By induction on N, Σ_{j=0}^{N} Y_j(ω) = X(ω) − A_N(ω): for N = 0 this is the hypothesis on Y_0, and Σ_{j=0}^{N+1} Y_j(ω) = (X(ω) − A_N(ω)) + (A_N(ω) − A_{N+1}(ω)) = X(ω) − A_{N+1}(ω) (Finset.sum_range_succ).
9. (A_N(ω) → 0.) By steps 5 and 6, |A_N(ω)| ≤ c_ω·μ({d < r_N}).toReal. Since μ({d < r_N}) → 0 and toReal is continuous at 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal), c_ω·μ({d < r_N}).toReal → c_ω·0 = 0, so A_N(ω) → 0 (squeeze_zero_norm).
10. ((b) HasSum.) By steps 8 and 9, Σ_{j<N+1} Y_j(ω) = X(ω) − A_N(ω) → X(ω) as N → ∞; shifting the index (tendsto_add_atTop_iff_nat 1), the partial sums Σ_{j<N} Y_j(ω) tend to X(ω). As (Y_j(ω))_j is summable (step 7), Summable.hasSum_iff_tendsto_nat gives HasSum (j ↦ Y_j(ω)) (X(ω)). This is (b).
11. (Vanishing lemma.) Since μ(ℝ^P \ spt X) = 0, μ-a.e. x lies in spt X (measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem). Let G be Borel, F ⊆ ℝ^P with G ⊆ F, and ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω disjoint from spt X ∩ F. For μ⌞G-a.e. x we have x ∈ G (ae_restrict_mem) and x ∈ spt X (ae_restrict_of_ae), hence x ∈ spt X ∩ F, x ∉ tsupport ω, ω(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and f_ω(x) = ξ(x)(0) = 0. Hence ∫_G f_ω dμ = 0 (integral_eq_zero_of_ae).
12. ((c) Supports.) spt X is closed by S (ii) and {r_j ≤ d} is closed, so K_j := spt X ∩ {r_j ≤ d} is closed. If tsupport ω is disjoint from K_j, then Y_j(ω) = ∫_{E_j} f_ω dμ = 0 by step 11 with G := E_j ⊆ F := {r_j ≤ d} (step 4); so spt Y_j ⊆ K_j by S (i). If tsupport ω is disjoint from spt X = spt X ∩ ℝ^P, then A_j(ω) = ∫_{d<r_j} f_ω dμ = 0 by step 11 with G := {d < r_j} and F := ℝ^P; so spt A_j ⊆ spt X by S (i) (spt X closed). This is (c). ∎
proof_key_steps: Each test form is bounded, |ω(x)| ≤ c_ω, so f_ω = ξ(ω) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, bounded and μ-integrable.
integral_add_compl and setIntegral_sdiff give Y_j(ω) = ∫_{E_j} ξ(ω) dμ over the half-open shells E_j.
The E_j are pairwise disjoint Borel sets; ML gives M(Y_j) ≤ μ(E_j) and M(A_j) ≤ μ({d < r_j}).
EB with ML: |Y_j(ω)| ≤ c_ω μ(E_j) and |A_N(ω)| ≤ c_ω μ({d < r_N}); Σ μ(E_j) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) < ∞ gives summability.
Partial sums telescope to X(ω) − A_N(ω) → X(ω), hence HasSum.
μ is carried by spt X, so the integrands vanish a.e. when tsupport ω misses spt X ∩ {r_j ≤ d}; S (i), (ii) give the supports.

audit.reason: The proof establishes boundedness, measurable integrands and integrability before subtracting integrals. The half-open shells are measurable and disjoint without requiring null level sets. ML and EB yield absolute summability and a vanishing remainder; telescoping then proves HasSum. Concentration and S give both support conclusions. Every stated conclusion follows.
